title: A Pen point lands on the grid line you can see
goal: An icon is drawn on a grid, and a Pen point ignores the grid completely. Switch Snap to Grid on, draw a box with the Rectangle tool and its edges catch the lines; draw the same box with the Pen and every point lands wherever the pointer was, so the outline is a fraction of a pixel off on all four sides and the icon is soft at every size. Make a Pen point catch the same lines a drag catches, with the same escape: hold Command and it goes exactly where you put it.
notes:
Verified 2026-09-13: Sources/Photonz/CanvasPen.swift contains no reference to snap or grid (grep for 'snap' and 'grid' in that file returns nothing), while CanvasView.canvasSnapSpacing (Sources/Photonz/CanvasView.swift:1425) is what drags and nudges pull to, fed by CanvasGrid.snapSpacing(atZoom:) (Sources/PhotonzCore/CanvasGrid.swift:190). So the plumbing already exists and the Pen simply does not call it.

Read the comment above snapSpacing before changing anything: the rule is that a drag only ever lands on a line the canvas is actually drawing at this zoom, because pulling to invisible lines is what made snapping feel broken before. A Pen point must obey the same rule.

The Command escape is the existing one, so find how a drag reads it rather than inventing a second modifier.

This serves the pen the user asked for on 2026-09-13 for building elaborate SVG icons: an icon that is off the grid is soft at every size it is used.
acceptance: With next-pen on, the grid visible and Snap to Grid on, clicking near a grid crossing puts the point exactly on it, and the preview shows it land there before the click commits
Holding Command while clicking places the point exactly under the pointer, the same escape a drag has
The pull handles from a press-and-drag point snap the same way, or the task says in its log why they deliberately do not
With the grid off, or Snap to Grid off, the Pen behaves exactly as it does today
Closing a path by clicking the first point still works when both points are snapped
A walk draws a snapped square with the Pen and checks the four corner coordinates are whole grid steps, and it passes twice on its own
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: review before building: the pull already exists (CanvasNSView.canvasNudgeGrid, the same value the arrow keys and every drag read), so the whole job is the Pen calling it. Kept it to the grid ONLY: the text click also takes pinned guides, but acceptance says the Pen must behave exactly as today with the grid off, and guide catching would break that.

review found a real trap the task did not mention: wouldClose/wouldFinish measured the RAW pointer against the anchor, 8 screen points. Half a cell is wider than that, so on a 32 grid a click 15 points from the first corner snapped exactly onto it and was NOT read as closing: the path took a second anchor on top of the first and never closed. Fixed by measuring where the click would LAND rather than where the pointer is, so the grid widens closing instead of breaking it. Test: aClickTheGridWouldPutOnTheFirstPointClosesThePath.

handles deliberately do NOT snap (acceptance item 3 allows this with a reason). A handle end is not a point on the outline, it is how hard the curve bends there; on a 32pt grid every curve would bend in whole cells and a handle shorter than half a cell would collapse to zero, throwing away the curve just pulled. It IS measured from the anchor's snapped home, so the curve hangs off the right place (test: theHandlePulledOutOfASnappedPointIsMeasuredFromWhereItLanded).

shift: the angle owns the point, as it does for every constrained drag, so the grid only takes the axis the angle left free. A level run from a point already on a line ends on a crossing; a 45 keeps its 45. snappedToFortyFive now rounds a negligible component to exact zero so an upright run is really upright and the axis test can tell.

code: PenSession.grid (NudgeGrid) + PenSession.free + place()/onGrid() in Sources/PhotonzCore/PenDrawing.swift; the canvas feeds both on press, drag, move, release and flagsChanged (CanvasPen.swift, CanvasPointerCue.swift). No release fork was needed: the Pen is shared code behind next-pen, which only Next has on.

verified: 12 new tests in PenDrawingTests (46 in the suite), Scripts/test.sh green at 6367 tests; Scripts/playtest/pen-on-the-grid-walk.json passes and was run three times (alone, in the pen sweep, in the grid sweep); the 17 grid walks, 9 pen walks and 5 path walks all pass. Screen Recording was granted, so the audit carries real window captures.

left rough and filed: the-grid-line-under-a-pen-point-lights-up-while (p2). The handle question rides on the audit's own line rather than a task, because it is a question for the user rather than work.

Pen points snap to the visible grid: PenSession.grid/free + place() in PhotonzCore, fed by CanvasNSView.canvasNudgeGrid. Command places exactly, handles deliberately unsnapped, closing measured at the landing point so half a cell no longer breaks it. 12 new unit tests, Scripts/test.sh green (6367), pen-on-the-grid-walk passes three times, grid/pen/path sweeps green.
